trigger: In a 3-node mini cluster, a follower that missed a new epoch rejoins and gets a DIFF. It crashes after it has appended and fsynced the new-epoch transactions during NEWLEADER handling, but before it writes currentEpoch. A test-subclass writeLongToFile throws before any byte of currentEpoch(.tmp) is written, which leaves the same disk state as a kill -9 or power loss at that point. The node is then restarted normally.
reason: Learner.syncWithLeader's NEWLEADER branch makes the new-epoch txns durable first (fzk.appendRequest + fzk.getZKDatabase().commit(), Learner.java:798-804) and only afterwards calls self.setCurrentEpoch(newEpoch) (Learner.java:813). These are two separate durable steps, and that order was chosen on purpose for ZOOKEEPER-4643/4785. A crash between them leaves committed epoch-N txns on disk, currentEpoch = N-1 and no currentEpoch.tmp. On restart, QuorumPeer.loadDataBase (QuorumPeer.java:1226-1238) only recovers through the .tmp file from ZOOKEEPER-4269. Otherwise it throws IOException('The current epoch, 1, is older than the last zxid ...'), and QuorumPeer.start fails on every restart. The state is consistent: the txns are ones the leader committed and the follower had not ACKed NEWLEADER. So the check rejects a state the protocol itself produces and permanently removes a voter until an operator edits currentEpoch by hand. The fault is a crash between two separate persistence steps, not inside one atomic step, so the trigger is realistic.
summary: A follower that crashes between persisting the synced new-epoch txns and writing currentEpoch can never restart ('current epoch is older than the last zxid') without manual repair.
